books.title: Both Can Be True
books.author: Jules Machias
books.why: The title itself names the theme: For someone who cycles through genders, Ash finds some days undoubtedly girl, but other times, 100 percent guy, and the story insists neither feeling cancels the other out. In parallel, Daniel lacks control of his emotions and has been told he's overly sensitive more times than he can count, wishing someone would accept him for it — his sensitivity is framed as both a struggle and a genuine strength. As the two kids rescue a dog that's about to be euthanized and bond over their secret, the book repeatedly shows that a person can hold seemingly contradictory truths about identity and emotion at the same time, both being real.

books.title: Grumpy Monkey
books.author: Suzanne Lang
books.why: Jim Panzee is having a wonderful day, but he still feels grumpy — and every friend he asks insists that if his day is good, he can't possibly be grumpy, so he should just smile. By the end, his friend Norman simply accepts that Jim can be having a great day AND feel grumpy, with no contradiction that needs fixing, modeling exactly the idea that two opposite-seeming feelings can both be true at once.

books.title: In My Heart: A Book of Feelings
books.author: Jo Witek (illustrated by Christine Roussey)
books.why: The narrator walks through paired, seemingly opposite feelings — brave and scared, calm and furious — describing moments where two emotions show up together, like feeling excited and nervous on the same day. Rather than resolving these into one 'correct' feeling, the book normalizes sitting with both at once, which is a gentle, very literal introduction to holding two true feelings simultaneously.

books.title: Ish
books.author: Peter Reynolds
books.why: After a harsh comment makes Ramon believe his drawings are technically wrong, his sister Marisol reframes his work as 'vase-ish' or 'tree-ish' rather than exact. The story lets both ideas coexist — a drawing can be imprecise/not realistic AND still be beautiful and worth making — teaching kids that accuracy and value aren't mutually exclusive.

books.title: Sometimes I'm Bombaloo
books.author: Rachel Vail
books.why: Katie describes herself as a good, gentle girl most of the time, but when she loses her temper she becomes 'Bombaloo,' someone wild and out of control. The book doesn't ask her to choose one identity; it lets both be genuinely true about the same child at different moments, showing kids that being generally kind and sometimes overwhelmed by anger aren't contradictions that cancel each other out.
